spec.title: Terminal Context Boundary — Frame's context follows Frame's terminal

tasks.title: Add pure `src/main/launchEnv.js` with `frameBinDir`, idempotent `prependFrameBin` and `supportsWrappers`
tasks.whatChanged: New pure module src/main/launchEnv.js exporting supportsWrappers(platform), frameBinDir(projectPath) and prependFrameBin(pathValue, projectPath, platform). It requires only node:path and frameConstants — no fs, no Electron. Nothing consumes it yet; T09 wires it into the PTY spawn env.
tasks.whyChanged: PATH composition is the one piece of this spec that is pure logic, so it was extracted rather than inlined into pty.js/ptyManager.js, which the testing record says stay untested. supportsWrappers() is the single POSIX gate so no call site does its own process.platform check. prependFrameBin drops any later copy of the bin dir instead of returning early on a match anywhere: a real `claude` earlier on PATH would win and the session would silently lose Frame's context, so the entry must be first, not merely present.

tasks.title: Add `test/launchEnv.test.js` covering idempotent prepending, the platform separator and an untouched PATH off-POSIX
tasks.whatChanged: 12 cases in test/launchEnv.test.js: frameBinDir with and without a project, the POSIX gate, prepend puts the bin dir first, prepending twice is a no-op, an entry sitting behind /usr/local/bin is moved rather than duplicated, the win32 PATH comes back byte-identical, an absent PATH becomes just the bin dir, and empty segments are dropped.
tasks.whyChanged: The purity case does more than grep the source: it reloads the module through a poisoned Module._load that throws on fs/electron and then exercises prependFrameBin, so a require added later fails the test rather than passing a string match. The move-not-duplicate case is the one that would otherwise regress quietly — a present-but-not-first entry still loses to a real CLI earlier on PATH.

tasks.title: Rewrite `getWrapperTemplate` to be recursion-safe and emit its tool's flags
tasks.whatChanged: The wrapper now resolves the real CLI at run time with its own directory filtered out of PATH (`PATH="$(path_without_self)" command -v <tool>`) and execs "$REAL_CLI", so a wrapper named after its tool cannot re-enter itself. It builds a frame_args array from the injection record — promptFlag in front of the preamble or the preamble positionally, settingsFlag appended only when that file exists — and keeps `exec "$REAL_CLI" "$@"` when the preamble is missing. A missing CLI exits 127 with a named message instead of looping.
tasks.whyChanged: Resolution is at run time rather than baked in at write time so a version-manager switch or reinstall is picked up immediately; an absolute path written at project open would go stale silently. The settings flag is conditional on the file existing because the payload is optional while the preamble is not. Deviation from plan.md's sequencing: the three existing wrapper assertions in test/frameTemplates.test.js asserted the old `exec codex ...` shape and were updated here rather than in T04 — a rewrite that leaves the suite red is not a finished task. T04 still adds the four new cases.

verification.detail: 435/435 pass; wrapper also exercised end-to-end in a sandbox — self-exec, arg passthrough, missing preamble, missing settings, absent CLI

tasks.title: Extend `test/frameTemplates.test.js` with the wrapper cases
tasks.whatChanged: Six cases added: declared flags appear and undeclared ones do not (a codex-style wrapper must not acquire Claude's flags), the script never execs the CLI by name, and four executed cases that stage a wrapper plus a fake real CLI in a temp dir and run it with .frame/bin first on PATH — no self-exec, `--resume/-p` passthrough, a missing preamble degrading to the bare CLI, and the settings flag skipped when the file is absent.
tasks.whyChanged: Success criterion 3 asks for a test that would hang or loop if the wrapper re-entered itself, which no string match can provide — so these four run bash for real, under a 10s execFileSync timeout so a recursion regression fails the suite instead of wedging it. They are skipped off-POSIX, where Frame writes no wrappers at all.

tasks.title: Write launch assets for every tool and expose `refreshLaunchAssets(projectPath)`
tasks.whatChanged: aiToolManager now writes a wrapper for every configured tool (Claude included, custom tools included) behind launchEnv.supportsWrappers(), alongside a per-tool preamble file and, for a tool declaring settingsFlag, its settings file. New writeIfChanged skips identical content; new prepareLaunchAssets(projectPath, tool) is the single writer; new refreshLaunchAssets(projectPath) walks every tool and is non-fatal per tool. getLaunchCommand now goes through prepareLaunchAssets and keeps composing flags as before — T07 changes what it returns.
tasks.whyChanged: Deviation from plan.md: the preamble is now `.frame/runtime/preamble-<tool>.txt`, not the single preamble.txt. The preamble differs by tool (a native reader gets different text), so one shared file meant whichever tool launched last decided what the next one read — tolerable while Frame composed every launch, wrong now that a tool can be hand-typed with no launch to rewrite the file first. Settings files follow the same rule, and `claude-settings.json` is what `${id}-settings.json` produces for Claude, so no existing path moved.

verification.detail: 441/441 pass; refreshLaunchAssets exercised against a temp project — 3 wrappers at 0755, 3 per-tool preambles, no rewrite on a second open

tasks.title: Refresh launch assets on project open
tasks.whatChanged: frameProject's CHECK_IS_FRAME_PROJECT handler now calls aiToolManager.refreshLaunchAssets(projectPath) beside gitSharing.ensureOnOpen and instructionDiscovery.refresh, gated on isFrame and wrapped non-fatally. Init's own loop — which wrote codex/gemini wrappers directly from getWrapperTemplate — was replaced by the same call.
tasks.whyChanged: Beyond the task as written: init had a second wrapper generator that knew nothing about injection records, so a freshly initialized project and a re-opened one would have produced different wrappers until the first open. One generator, or the shapes drift — which is the exact failure this spec exists to close. Both call sites are lazy requires, since aiToolManager pulls telemetry and init's module graph is deliberately flat.

tasks.title: Dispatch through the wrapper on POSIX
tasks.whatChanged: getLaunchCommand now returns `./.frame/bin/<id>` with no Frame flags of its own for every tool on POSIX, and falls back to the bare command plus inline flags where no wrapper exists. New wrapperLaunchCommand() and bareCommandFor() are the one place that choice is made, and CHECK_AI_TOOL_AVAILABLE composes its dispatched line from the same helper. Claude gained fallbackCommand: 'claude'.
tasks.whyChanged: The dispatched command is a relative path, not the bare name: a bare `claude` would resolve through PATH to the same wrapper once T09 lands, and Frame's flags would stack on the wrapper's. Beyond the task as written, the availability handler had to move too — it, not getLaunchCommand, composes the line agentDispatch actually types, so leaving it on tool.command would have made the two disagree. Claude's fallbackCommand exists so the probe still asks whether the real CLI is installed instead of stopping at the wrapper it always finds.

verification.detail: 441/441 pass; all three tools verified to compose ./.frame/bin/<id> with a dispatch's extra flags appended
